name: Hard mewing

card.summary: Mewing with deliberate upward tongue pressure; discussed as a stronger version of tongue posture, with no research testing it and some users reporting masseter growth.
card.note: No published study has tested it; users report enlarged masseters and tooth gaps in combination with other practices.

quick.overview:
Hard mewing is a looksmaxxing term for pressing the tongue against the palate with deliberate force, as opposed to the light resting posture usually described as mewing. It is discussed on looksmax.org alongside chewing, thumb pulling, chin tucks and palate expansion.

Proponents report forward growth, a wider jaw and better breathing and posture. No published study has examined forceful tongue pressure as an appearance practice, and orthodontic bodies say mewing in general lacks evidence.
quick.mechanism: Believers say stronger and more sustained pressure from the tongue on the palate drives more bone remodelling than a relaxed resting posture, extending the orthotropic idea that tongue posture guides upper-jaw growth. Mechanical-loading research shows bone adapts to strain in general, but no study measures what tongue pressure does to the adult facial skeleton.
quick.risks: Users on forums report that hard mewing made their masseter muscles wider, changed how their cheeks looked and, in combination with thumb pulling and expanders, opened a gap between the front teeth. These are anecdotal reports. No clinical data exist on forceful tongue pressure.

lead: Hard mewing is a term used in looksmaxxing communities for a more forceful form of mewing, in which a person presses the tongue upward against the palate with deliberate effort rather than simply resting it there [1][2]. Forum users use it interchangeably with, or as a stage beyond, ordinary mewing, and some threads ask directly how the two differ [3].

Mewing derives from orthotropics, developed by British orthodontist John Mew, which claims that tongue posture guides facial growth. Professional orthodontic bodies do not support that claim, and the American Association of Orthodontists has stated there is no evidence that mewing improves the jaw [4][5]. No published research addresses hard mewing specifically.
infobox: Chin tucks, chewing, thumb pulling, palate expansion

paras: In forum usage, hard mewing means pushing the tongue firmly into the roof of the mouth, sometimes while keeping the lips sealed and the teeth together, in contrast to a relaxed resting posture [3]. Some users describe doing it continuously during the day, often combined with chin tucks and other 'bonehacks' [6][7].

No studies found. No clinical study has examined forceful tongue pressure on the palate for facial appearance. The wider topic of mewing and orthotropics has one small twin study of professionally delivered orthotropic treatment and a 2019 commentary, neither of which tests hard mewing [1][4].

On looksmax.org, hard mewing is both promoted and disputed. One poster claimed it gave forward growth even after puberty when combined with chin tucks and sprinting, calling it more effective than drugs, while replies asked for photographic evidence [8]. Another thread describes a user who began hard mewing and noticed wider masseters, hollower cheeks and a harder time resting the teeth together, and asked whether an overbite was responsible [9]. A third user lists hard mewing, chewing, thumb pulling, belt pulling, bonesmashing and chin tucking as parts of a daily regimen [10]. A further thread asks what to do about a gap between the front teeth after palate expansion, thumb pulling and hard mewing [11].

The discussion shows the belief that more force means more effect, and an opposing view in other threads that it is unproven or counterproductive; one thread title urges members to stop hard mewing [12].

lore.intro: Hard mewing appears on looksmax.org as the intensive version of mewing, usually in routines with other bone-related practices [6][10].

claims.claim: Hard mewing causes forward growth even after puberty
claims.believers: A poster says it gave substantial forward growth after puberty when combined with chin tucks and sprinting, and others report multi-year routines [8][10].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined it; the AAO says there is no evidence that mewing improves the jaw [5].

claims.claim: Hard mewing widens the jaw or enlarges the masseters
claims.believers: A user reports that masseters became wider after starting hard mewing, which he regards as a mixed result [9].
claims.experts: Masseter enlargement is documented in people who clench or grind their teeth or chew constantly, but no study links it to tongue pressure [13].

claims.claim: Hard mewing combined with thumb pulling and expanders produces visible change
claims.believers: Members describe combined regimens, and one asks about a diastema after combining the practices [10][11].
claims.experts: Palatal expansion is an orthodontic treatment with known side effects including a gap between upper front teeth; it uses appliances, not tongue pressure [14].
